claim: The Department of Justice does not seek to stop any ballot from being cast or to stop the certification of Alaska's election.
read: Attorney General Todd Blanche posted that the Justice Department does not seek to stop the certification of Alaska's election. The department's complaint in United States v. Alaska asks the court to enjoin the state from certifying any result that may be impacted by voter confusion. The complaint defines that impact as a case where Senator Dan S. Sullivan does not win, but would have won if every vote for Daniel J. Sullivan had gone to him instead. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the conditional nature of the requested order. The missing fact is that the complaint seeks to block certification in the specific scenario where the incumbent loses narrowly.

sources.title: U.S. District Court for the District of Alaska — Complaint, United States v. State of Alaska, 3:26-cv-00376
Attorney General Todd Blanche — X post

script: Late Check. The attorney general said the Justice Department does not seek to stop the certification of Alaska's election. The department's own complaint asks a federal court to block the state from certifying any result that may be impacted by voter confusion. The complaint defines that impact as a case where Senator Dan Sullivan does not win, but would have if every vote for the other Daniel Sullivan had gone to him. The prayer for relief seeks an injunction against certification pending an investigation into whether those votes were meant for the incumbent. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: It looked like another rigged election, frankly.
read: Speaking to reporters Monday before a Mississippi rally, the president said Brazil's presidential runoff looked like another rigged election and had a terrible look, citing the tabulation and a last-minute voting extension. Brazil's Superior Electoral Court reported the official result: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva 64,256,232 votes (51.79 percent), Flávio Bolsonaro 59,826,041 votes (48.21 percent), a margin of more than 4.4 million. Independent analyses of TSE data found roughly 34,000 to 35,000 votes cast after the original 5 p.m. close, about 0.03 percent of the total, far smaller than the margin. The TSE president, appointed by Jair Bolsonaro, said the extension did not affect the outcome. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the last-minute extension ordered by a Supreme Court justice. The missing fact is that the extra votes were too few to change the result.

script: Evening Check. A reporter asked the president if Brazil's election was fair. He said it looked terrible and looked like another rigged election. Brazil's Superior Electoral Court certified Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva with 64,256,232 votes, 51.79 percent, over Flávio Bolsonaro's 59,826,041 votes, 48.21 percent. The margin was more than four million votes. A Supreme Court order extended voting by two hours. Analyses of the official data show about 34,000 votes after the original close, 0.03 percent of the total. The electoral court president said the extension did not change the result. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: Minnesota voters are choosing a GHOST CANDIDATE who is NOT REAL. "Ilhan Omar" as it appears on the ballot is not a real person!!
read: A high-engagement post claims voters are choosing a ghost candidate and that the name Ilhan Omar on the ballot is not a real person. A federal court filing in the search-warrant matter lists the subject as Congresswoman Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar. a/k/a means also known as. The filing does not find that the ballot name is nonexistent. Official House records, the Biographical Directory, and her office site list her as Ilhan Omar, the sitting Representative from Minnesota's 5th District. Her office has stated that Ilhan Omar is her real name. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the alternate name in the motion. The missing fact is that a/k/a is not a finding of a fake ballot identity.

claim: Everyone thought she came in second or third, but then she 'won.'
read: In a Saturday-night Truth Social post, the president wrote that Lisa Murkowski only got elected because of ranked-choice voting and that everyone thought she came in second or third before she won. The official 2022 Alaska Division of Elections first-choice tally shows Murkowski finishing first with 113,495 votes (43.37 percent) to Kelly Tshibaka's 111,480 (42.60 percent). She led the initial count by roughly 2,000 votes; second-choice ballots from eliminated candidates then expanded her margin to 53.7 percent. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the ranked-choice redistribution. The missing fact is that she already held the plurality before any redistribution.

script: Morning Check. A Truth Social post says everyone thought Lisa Murkowski came in second or third, then she won under ranked-choice voting. The official first-choice tally from the Alaska Division of Elections shows she finished first with 113,495 votes, 43.37 percent, ahead of Kelly Tshibaka at 111,480 votes, 42.60 percent. She led the initial count. Second-choice ballots from the Democrat and a withdrawn Republican then widened the margin to 53.7 percent. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.
